snapshot.what_it_does: Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) is a diversified Indian company whose portfolio spans Digital Services (Jio telecom/digital), Retail, Media & Entertainment, Oil to Chemicals (O2C), Oil and Gas, and New Energy businesses. It delivered record consolidated revenue of ₹11,75,919 crore (US$ 124.0 billion) and EBITDA of ₹2,07,911 crore (US$ 21.9 billion) in FY 2025-26, driven by double-digit growth in Digital Services, Retail and Media & Entertainment.

segments.name: Digital Services (Jio)
segments.note: Gross revenue ₹1,76,164 crore; EBITDA ₹76,560 crore, up 17.8% Y-o-Y; 268 million 5G subscribers; ~13 million JioAirFiber premises

segments.name: Retail
segments.note: Gross revenue ₹3,71,085 crore, up 12.1%; EBITDA ₹27,034 crore, up 7.7%; 387 million registered customers; 1.9 billion+ annual transactions

segments.name: Media & Entertainment
segments.note: EBITDA up 218.7% with record viewership and double-digit revenue growth

segments.name: Oil to Chemicals (O2C)
segments.note: EBITDA up 10.1% via higher operating rates, optimised feedstock sourcing and higher domestic placements

segments.name: Oil and Gas
segments.note: EBITDA down 10.1% on natural decline in KG D6 production and softer gas prices

snapshot.geographies: Primarily India-based operations with exports of ₹2,78,808 crore; subsidiaries span Singapore, USA, Malaysia, Middle East (DMCC) and other international locations (related-party disclosures).
key_facts: Consolidated revenue ₹11,75,919 crore (US$ 124.0 billion), up 9.8% Y-o-Y
EBITDA ₹2,07,911 crore (US$ 21.9 billion), up 13.4% Y-o-Y; PAT ₹95,754 crore (US$ 10.1 billion), up 17.8%
Net debt ₹1,24,717 crore (US$ 13.2 billion); gross debt ₹3,74,421 crore as of March 31, 2026
Capex ₹1,44,271 crore (US$ 15.2 billion), funded by cash profits, directed to O2C, New Energy, Digital Services and Retail
Recommended dividend of ₹6 per share (₹8,119 crore); JV with Meta (₹855 crore, 70:30) for enterprise AI solutions

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Credibility is mixed: near-term momentum and Jio margin/FMCG scale claims were broadly borne out, but several dated operational targets are not explicitly confirmed later. Reported figures are mostly consistent, though PAT volatility in Q4 FY26 (-12.6%) and Q1 FY27 (-22.4%) tempers a clean high score.

rows.promise: Retail de-merger, NCLT approved, to happen in November 2025 pending written judgment.
rows.delivered: Later calls treat RCPL as demerged: Q4 retail adjusted for RCPL; Q1 FY27 RCPL revenue ₹8,600 Cr, 2x YoY. November date not stated.
rows.cite: Q4 FY26 reported; Q1 FY27 reported

rows.promise: Home broadband digitization run-rate of about 1 million homes/month expected to continue and keep growing.
rows.delivered: No later call gives home-premise run-rate; only Q2 itself reported 23M fixed-broadband premises, +3M QoQ.

rows.promise: Jio margins should improve as network and assets are monetized more.
rows.delivered: Q4 RJIL margin 56.2% (+230 bps); Q1 FY27 JPL margin 53.3% versus Q3 51.8%, EBITDA +15.1%.
rows.cite: Q4 FY26 reported; Q1 FY27 reported

rows.promise: Beverage capacity to more than double this year; Kurnool plant ready by March; food parks begin next quarter.
rows.delivered: FMCG scaled: FY26 ₹22,000 Cr, Q4 ₹7,350 Cr ~2x; Q1 FY27 RCPL ₹8,600 Cr 2x. Capacity/Kurnool not stated.
rows.cite: Q4 FY26 reported; Q1 FY27 reported

rows.promise: Quick commerce is very much on track to become the second-largest QC player.
rows.delivered: Q3 reported 1.6M December orders; later calls give no QC market rank, only Ajio Rush orders +136% QoQ.
rows.cite: Q3 FY26 reported; Q1 FY27 reported

rows.promise: Fuel cracks expected to remain strong for some time on refinery damage and shipping concerns.
rows.delivered: Q1 FY27 reported revenue +25% on oil prices; O2C revenue +30%, EBITDA ₹17,000 Cr, +17% YoY.

rows.promise: AI-first network automation and energy optimization should show good results in coming quarters.
rows.delivered: Q1 FY27 JPL revenue +11.8%, EBITDA +15.1%, margin 53.3%, ARPU ₹215.6; AI-specific attribution not stated.

rows.promise: Grow online rapidly in FY27 via dark stores, omni-channel and JioMart, with positive unit economics, funded from profits.
rows.delivered: FY27 incomplete; Q2 FY27 actuals show consolidated revenue +28.6%, PAT +40.6%, but no online unit-economics disclosure.

bull.point: Jio EBITDA ₹76,560 crore (+17.8%) with 268 million 5G subscribers; Retail gross revenue ₹3,71,085 crore (+12.1%), 387 million registered customers.
Net debt ₹1,24,717 crore versus ₹2,07,911 crore EBITDA; ₹1,44,271 crore capex was funded by cash profits; dividend ₹6/share.

bear.point: PAT is volatile: Q4 FY26 fell 12.6% and Q1 FY27 fell 22.4% despite revenue growth, before Q2 FY27 rebounded 40.6%.
Margins compressed into FY27: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 14.8%/operating 9.8%, Q1 FY27 15.2%/10.3%, below Q2 FY27 16.9%/12.3%.
Gross debt ₹3,74,421 crore and capex ₹1,44,271 crore are sizable; Oil & Gas EBITDA fell 10.1% on KG D6 decline and softer gas.

watch: Whether Q2 FY27 PAT +40.6% and 16.9%/12.3% margins hold after Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27 PAT declines.
Jio ARPU ₹215.6 and 53.3% margin trend; Retail online positive unit economics remain not stated.
O2C cracks versus Oil & Gas KG D6 decline, alongside ₹1,44,271 crore capex and net debt trajectory.
